subject: Establishing internal-hostname trust graph + cert ops for outbound TLS proxying
messages:
From: Alice Huang <alice.huang@axioncloud.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@axioncloud.com
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment checklist - hostname/DNS & TLS handoff

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. As we start our on-prem pilot with Redwood Private, we want to lock down how internal hostnames map, who terminates TLS for private endpoints, and how cert provisioning will work for our air-gapped clusters. We attached a network map (axion_network_map_v2.pdf) and a short list of constraints:

- We run split-horizon DNS internally (internal names resolve differently inside our VPC).
- Egress to external services is through a controlled TLS proxy; we currently perform downstream TLS termination for third-party SaaS.
- We need cryptographic evidence and an ops runbook for cert rotation (auditable timeline).
- Some edge boxes are offline by design (no outbound ACME).

Can Redwood confirm recommended termination points (customer-side vs Redwood-side), mutual-TLS needs for service-to-service (Redwood runtime -> customer front door), and an approach for cert bootstrapping in air-gapped environments? We want proposed options for trade-offs (latency, key custody, auditability).

Appreciate any early thoughts — Alice
AxionCloud, Product Ops

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private deployment checklist - hostname/DNS & TLS handoff

Folks — my high-level take (networking-first):

1) Termination options (ranked):
   - Customer-edge termination (recommended for max data isolation): the customer's ingress (their LB or edge TLS proxy) terminates client TLS; Redwood connects outbound from the runtime to customer gateway using mutual-TLS or client certs. Pros: clear key custody, simple audit trail on customer side. Cons: higher latency for handshake and more customer ops required.

   - Split termination with mTLS at ingress + downstream TLS to service: TLS is terminated at the edge for client traffic, but we maintain mTLS between Redwood runtime and customer front-door to ensure authenticity. Pros: better inter-service auditing, lower exposure. Cons: operational complexity, cert distribution.

   - Redwood-side termination (only when customer permits): Redwood handles TLS and presents certs for private FQDNs. Pros: centralized ops, easier rotation. Cons: fails isolation requirements and key custody concerns.

2) DNS: keep split-horizon mapping authoritative on the customer side (they own internal namespace) and publish an SRV/CNAME mapping to a customer-controlled proxy reachable from Redwood. Avoid delegating parent zone to us. Use short TTLs during rollouts.

3) Air-gapped bootstrap: recommended approach is an offline CA + signed CSRs shipped via secure artifact (signed and recorded in audit). We should document: CSR generation, manual signing, and automated local distribution with checksums.

I'll draft a network diagram overlay showing where mTLS lives.

— Jonas (Infra SRE)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, jonas.weber@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2026 09:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private deployment checklist - hostname/DNS & TLS handoff

Adding cert ops details and an ops-runbook outline. Key points:

- Certificate types: client TLS certs for runtime -> customer gateway (mTLS), server certs for customer-facing endpoints, and signing certs for offline CA.
- Provisioning model options:
   A) Customer-managed ACME / automated (fast, but requires outbound access).
   B) Redwood-managed issuance with customer KMS for private-key escrow (compromise: Redwood orchestrates but keys live in customer KMS/HSM).
   C) Offline CA model (air-gapped): we provide the tooling (CSR packager, validation checklist) and customer runs signing; they ship signed cert and fingerprint back.

- Rotation policy: recommend 90-day server certs for public-facing hostnames, 180-day for mTLS certs with automatic revocation hooks into both Redwood & customer ops. Include audit events for: CSR created, CSR signed, cert shipped, cert installed, and cert revoked.

- Runbook sections: preflight (DNS proof, key custody confirmation), CSR flow (commands, expected outputs), emergency rotation steps, and audit log queries.

Draft attached: proposed_cert_ops_runbook.md

— Marissa, Product Security
Attachment: proposed_cert_ops_runbook.md
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, jonas.weber@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 19 Aug 2026 14:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private deployment checklist - hostname/DNS & TLS handoff

Couple of practical notes from model-serving and runtime perspective:

- DNS resolution: Redwood runtime instances should be able to resolve customer-internal hostnames when outbound requests are necessary (e.g., webhooks, callbacks). We should avoid stuffing customer private zones into our global resolver; instead create per-deployment per-tenant resolvers or forwarders (stub zones) that point at customer authoritative DNS inside their VPC. This reduces risk of leaking private names.

- ACME sidecar pattern: for networks with outbound connectivity, run a small sidecar container that performs ACME + cert reloads locally. For air-gapped workloads, we fall back to the offline-CSR flow Marissa suggested. I sketched an ACME-sidecar-diagram.png (attached).

- SNI mapping & routing: require a short-lived mapping table that maps internal FQDN -> connection endpoint + cert fingerprint. This table is versioned and signed by Redwood and can live in the deployment control plane for fast rollbacks.

Operational ask: we need a single sentence for the customer listing the three options (edge-terminate, mTLS split, Redwood-terminate) and what customer must provide for each (DNS delegation, KMS access, CSR archive). I can convert to a table for the response.

— Karthik, Runtime Engineering
Attachment: acme-sidecar-diagram.png

Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment checklist - hostname/DNS & TLS handoff

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear constraints and network map. Internal summary and recommended path (short):

Recommendation (preferred): Customer-edge termination with mTLS between Redwood runtime and customer front-door (option: mutual TLS using customer-managed KMS for private keys).

Why: preserves customer key custody, easiest for compliance audits, and keeps split-horizon DNS authoritative on the customer side. Our role is to provide tooling and an ops runbook:

What Redwood will deliver:
- Detailed ops runbook (attached) covering CSR packaging, signed artifact exchange, installation, rotation, and emergency revocation.
- ACME-sidecar for deployments that allow outbound connectivity (automated issuance + local reloads).
- Signed, versioned SNI->endpoint mapping manifest that both sides can verify during rollouts.
- Audit events publishing for CSR->sign->install lifecycle (we will forward logs to customer SOC via their preferred collector).

Fallback options: if customer prefers Redwood-terminated certs we support that under a special security agreement and customer KMS escrow. For fully air-gapped zones, we will use offline CA + signed CSR exchange.

Next steps:
1) Alice: confirm which option (edge-terminate with mTLS preferred) and provide preferred KMS vendor / whether you need Redwood-run signing automation.
2) We will deliver an internal draft of the combined diagram + runbook by EOD 8/27 and a customer-ready one by 8/30.

I attached the draft runbook and diagrams for your review. If ops@vigilant wants to join the runbook review, we can set a 30-min sync next week.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
